verses.en: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: so doth a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom and honour.
verses.pt: Assim como as moscas mortas fazem cheirar mal do óleo do perfumador, assim também um pouco de tolice se sobrepõe à sabedoria e honra.
verses.en_web: Dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to produce an evil odor; so does a little folly outweigh wisdom and honor.
verses.en_bbe: Dead flies make the oil of the perfumer give out an evil smell; more valued is a little wisdom than the great glory of the foolish.

verses.en: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand; but a fool’s heart at his left.
verses.pt: O coração do sábio está à sua direita; mas o coração do tolo está à sua esquerda.
verses.en_web: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand, but a fool’s heart at his left.
verses.en_bbe: The heart of the wise man goes in the right direction; but the heart of a foolish man in the wrong.

verses.en: Yea also, when he that is a fool walketh by the way, his wisdom faileth him, and he saith to every one that he is a fool.
verses.pt: E até quando o tolo vai pelo caminho, falta-lhe bom-senso em seu coração, e diz a todos que é ele é tolo.
verses.en_web: Yes also, when the fool walks by the way, his understanding fails him, and he says to everyone that he is a fool.
verses.en_bbe: And when the foolish man is walking in the way, he has no sense and lets everyone see that he is foolish.

verses.en: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for yielding pacifieth great offences.
verses.pt: Se o espírito de um chefe se levantar contra ti, não deixes teu lugar, porque a calma aquieta grandes ofensas.
verses.en_web: If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, don’t leave your place; for gentleness lays great offenses to rest.
verses.en_bbe: If the wrath of the ruler is against you, keep in your place; in him who keeps quiet even great sins may be overlooked.

verses.en: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, as an error which proceedeth from the ruler:
verses.pt: Há um mal que vi abaixo do sol, um tipo de erro que é proveniente dos que têm autoridade:
verses.en_web: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, the sort of error which proceeds from the ruler.
verses.en_bbe: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, like an error which comes by chance from a ruler:

verses.en: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.
verses.pt: Põem o tolo em cargos elevados, mas os ricos sentam em lugares baixos.
verses.en_web: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a low place.
verses.en_bbe: The foolish are placed in high positions, but men of wealth are kept low.

verses.en: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.
verses.pt: Vi servos a cavalo, e príncipes que andavam a pé como se fossem servos sobre a terra.
verses.en_web: I have seen servants on horses, and princes walking like servants on the earth.
verses.en_bbe: I have seen servants on horses, and rulers walking on the earth as servants.

verses.en: He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; and whoso breaketh an hedge, a serpent shall bite him.
verses.pt: Quem cavar uma cova, nela cairá; e quem romper um muro, uma cobra o morderá.
verses.en_web: He who digs a pit may fall into it; and whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
verses.en_bbe: He who makes a hole for others will himself go into it, and for him who makes a hole through a wall the bite of a snake will be a punishment.

verses.en: Whoso removeth stones shall be hurt therewith; and he that cleaveth wood shall be endangered thereby.
verses.pt: Quem extrai pedras, por elas será ferido; e quem parte lenha, correrá perigo por ela.
verses.en_web: Whoever carves out stones may be injured by them. Whoever splits wood may be endangered thereby.
verses.en_bbe: He who gets out stones from the earth will be damaged by them, and in the cutting of wood there is danger.

verses.en: If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom is profitable to direct.
verses.pt: Se o ferro está embotado, e não afiar o corte, então deve se pôr mais forças; mas a sabedoria é proveitosa para se ter sucesso.
verses.en_web: If the ax is blunt, and one doesn’t sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength; but skill brings success.
verses.en_bbe: If the iron has no edge, and he does not make it sharp, then he has to put out more strength; but wisdom makes things go well.

verses.en: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler is no better.
verses.pt: Se a cobra morder sem estar encantada, então proveito nenhum tem a fala do encantador.
verses.en_web: If the snake bites before it is charmed, then is there no profit for the charmer’s tongue.
verses.en_bbe: If a snake gives a bite before the word of power is said, then there is no longer any use in the word of power.

verses.en: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.
verses.pt: As palavras da boca do sábio são agradáveis; porém os lábios do tolo o devoram.
verses.en_web: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but a fool is swallowed by his own lips.
verses.en_bbe: The words of a wise man's mouth are sweet to all, but the lips of a foolish man are his destruction.

verses.en: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness: and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
verses.pt: O princípio das palavras de sua boca é tolice; e o fim de sua boca é uma loucura ruim.
verses.en_web: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
verses.en_bbe: The first words of his mouth are foolish, and the end of his talk is evil crime.

verses.en: A fool also is full of words: a man cannot tell what shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him?
verses.pt: O tolo multiplica as palavras, porém ninguém sabe o que virá no futuro; e quem lhe fará saber o que será depois dele?
verses.en_web: A fool also multiplies words. Man doesn’t know what will be; and that which will be after him, who can tell him?
verses.en_bbe: The foolish are full of words; man has no knowledge of what will be; and who is able to say what will be after him?

verses.en: The labour of the foolish wearieth every one of them, because he knoweth not how to go to the city.
verses.pt: O trabalho dos tolos lhes traz cansaço, porque não sabem ir à cidade.
verses.en_web: The labor of fools wearies every one of them; for he doesn’t know how to go to the city.
verses.en_bbe: The work of the foolish will be a weariness to him, because he has no knowledge of the way to the town.

verses.en: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!
verses.pt: Ai de ti, ó terra cujo rei é um menino, e cujos príncipes comem pela madrugada!
verses.en_web: Woe to you, land, when your king is a child, and your princes eat in the morning!
verses.en_bbe: Unhappy is the land whose king is a boy, and whose rulers are feasting in the morning.

verses.en: Blessed art thou, O land, when thy king is the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
verses.pt: Bem-aventurada é tu, ó terra, cujo rei é filho de nobres, e cujos príncipes comem no tempo devido, para se fortalecerem, e não para se embebedarem!
verses.en_web: Happy are you, land, when your king is the son of nobles, and your princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
verses.en_bbe: Happy is the land whose ruler is of noble birth, and whose chiefs take food at the right time, for strength and not for feasting.

verses.en: By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through.
verses.pt: Pela muita preguiça o teto se deteriora; e pala frouxidão das mãos a casa tem goteiras.
verses.en_web: By slothfulness the roof sinks in; and through idleness of the hands the house leaks.
verses.en_bbe: When no work is done the roof goes in, and when the hands do nothing water comes into the house.

verses.en: A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all things.
verses.pt: Para rir se fazem banquetes, e o vinho alegra aos vivos; mas o dinheiro responde por tudo.
verses.en_web: A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes the life glad; and money is the answer for all things.
verses.en_bbe: A feast is for laughing, and wine makes glad the heart; but by the one and the other money is wasted.

verses.en: Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.
verses.pt: Nem mesmo em pensamento amaldiçoes ao rei, nem também no interior de teu quarto amaldiçoes ao rico, porque as aves dos céus levam o que foi falado, e os que tem asas contam o que foi dito.
verses.en_web: Don’t curse the king, no, not in your thoughts; and don’t curse the rich in your bedroom: for a bird of the sky may carry your voice, and that which has wings may tell the matter.
verses.en_bbe: Say not a curse against the king, even in your thoughts; and even secretly say not a curse against the man of wealth; because a bird of the air will take the voice, and that which has wings will give news of it.
